headline: SURE-GRPO reports more efficient abstention on underspecified reasoning tasks
summary: The Oct. 13 v2 of a paper on SURE-GRPO adds an 8B reasoning model to the earlier 4B-model account and reports a revised average abstention-performance gain of 14.7% while retaining answerable-task capability and reducing chain-of-thought length by 44%. The method rewards models for identifying missing information and avoiding redundant reasoning. The paper evaluates six model families and fine-tunes four models against accuracy-only and accuracy-plus-length-penalty baselines. These are author-reported results; training and evaluation were not independently reproduced.
